Message from the Dean

Where innovation meets impact

Dr. Turki N. BaroudDean, KFUPM Business School

At KFUPM Business School, we are reimagining business education for a new era defined by innovation, technology, and purpose.

As Saudi Arabia advances toward Vision 2030, KBS is shaping leaders who can bridge business and technology, turning ideas into real-world impact. Our programs empower students to think strategically, act entrepreneurially, and lead responsibly in a fast-changing global economy.

We believe that true business leadership today requires fluency in data, technology, and systems thinking, coupled with a deep sense of purpose and responsibility toward society.

Our faculty combine world-class scholarship with industry engagement, ensuring that every course, project, and partnership connects classroom learning with real business challenges. Through our global collaborations and deep ties to industry, we are building a learning ecosystem that equips graduates not just to adapt to change but to lead it. KBS will continue to evolve, expanding interdisciplinary programs, advancing impactful research, and fostering an entrepreneurial mindset among students and executives alike.

Message from the Chairman

Thinking across boundaries

Dr. Nasser A. AlqahtaniChairman, Department of Management & Marketing

We are building a department where business disciplines meet technology and the behavioral sciences to prepare leaders for what comes next.

We bring together management, marketing, human resources, organizational behavior, strategy, entrepreneurship, innovation, and international business, because the challenges ahead will not respect traditional boundaries. Increasingly, our most exciting work happens where these fields intersect with technology and behavioral science.

Three commitments guide us. We deliver education that transforms, blending rigorous theory with hands-on practice. We conduct research that creates impact, as our faculty, postdoctoral researchers, and PhD students tackle real organizational challenges in the Kingdom and beyond. And we partner with organizations across the public, private, and nonprofit sectors to advance Vision 2030 and create lasting value.

Our strength lies in our people: curious students, dedicated faculty, professional staff, and committed partners. Together, we are shaping the talent, ideas, and partnerships the Kingdom will need in the decade ahead. Whether you are a prospective student, faculty member, partner, or alumnus, I warmly invite you to reach out.

Source: KBSBS Digital & Social Media Marketing03

Overview

BS Digital and Social Media Marketing

Future-focused program designed to prepare graduates for leadership in an AI-driven, data-centric, and platform-based business environment.

Source: KBSBS Digital & Social Media Marketing05
Overview

Program Overview

  • Integrates strong marketing foundations with advanced digital strategy, social media intelligence, consumer behavior analytics, and AI-enabled marketing technologies
  • Students develop the ability to design, implement, and evaluate digital marketing initiatives using real-time data from social platforms, web analytics, e-commerce systems, and performance dashboards
  • Not a traditional marketing degree with digital add-ons, but a comprehensive digital-first program that equips students to operate at the intersection of strategy, analytics, technology, and creativity
Disciplines and competencies covered
Marketing
New media
Crowd/consumer behavior
Artificial Intelligence
Quant/analytics/ computing
Source: KBSBS Digital & Social Media Marketing06
Program Learning Outcomes

Learning Objectives

Knowledge and UnderstandingSkillsValues, Autonomy, and Responsibility
01

Digital and Social Media Marketing Knowledge & Research

Ability to explain and apply digital social media marketing concepts, principles, and theories and to conduct market research

Knowledge and Understanding
Explain foundational concepts, theories, and contemporary industry / societal practices in digital and social media marketing
Skills
Students will be able to design and conduct digital and social media marketing research
02

Digital Platforms and Marketing Technologies

Students will demonstrate the ability to explain and analyze and utilize digital platforms, marketing technologies, and AI-enabled tools to support digital and social media marketing strategies

Knowledge and Understanding
Discuss the roles, functions, and strategic importance of digital platforms, marketing technologies, and AI-enabled tools used in digital and social media marketing
Skills
Students will be able to utilize and evaluate digital platforms, marketing technologies, and analytics tools to support digital and social media marketing strategies
Source: KBSBS Digital & Social Media Marketing07
Program Learning Outcomes · BS Digital and Social Media Marketing
03

Leadership in Digital and Social Media Marketing and Teamwork Abilities

Students will explain leadership principles and apply leadership skills and communicate effectively with teams addressing digital and social media marketing challenges

Knowledge and Understanding
Outline leadership principles frameworks in digital and social media marketing
Skills
Students will have the ability to work effectively in collaborative and inclusive teams to achieve common digital and social media marketing goals
Ability to communicate digital and social media marketing ideas effectively to diverse media platforms
04

Digital and Social Media Marketing Decision-Making Abilities

The ability to make informed business and ethical decisions

Knowledge and Understanding
Interpret qualitative and quantitative decision-making frameworks and their application in digital and social media marketing contexts
Skills
Students will apply critical thinking and structured problem-solving techniques/models to evaluate business situations and make evidence-based decisions that consider immediate and future implications
Values, Autonomy, and Responsibility
Students will be able to identify sustainability and ethical issues in digital and social media marketing and apply these as lenses in developing marketing solutions
Source: KBSBS Digital & Social Media Marketing08

BS Digital and Social Media Marketing · Practical training

Summer Training & Internship

Every student gains real workplace experience before graduating. The degree plan comes in two tracks, so you choose how you get it: a summer training placement or a full-semester internship.

Track 1
Summer Training
DSMM 399
1credit hour
128CR degree plan
When
The summer after the junior year
Prerequisites
ENGL 214 and DSMM 302; at least 65 credit hours completed
Track 2
Internship
DSMM 398
6credit hours
127CR degree plan
When
A full semester: senior year, semester 1
Prerequisites
ENGL 214, DSMM 302 and DSMM 330; at least 85 credit hours completed
Where it fits in the four years
SummerYear 1Year 2Year 3SummerYear 4
InternshipYear 1Year 2Year 3Y4 S1Y4 S2
Students put digital marketing, analytics and AI skills to work on real business problems in a professional setting. Both tracks also include the two-semester Senior Project (DSMM 411 & 412) in the senior year.

Fundamentals of Digital & Social Media Marketing

DSMM 302
Pre-requisiteMKT 250Topics14

  • Social Media Marketing Influencer Marketing
  • Search Engine Optimization (SEO)
  • Paid Media (Search & Display Advertising)

  • Digital Analytics

Consumer Behavior in the Digital Age

DSMM 305
Pre-requisiteMKT 250Topics9
  • Introduction to consumer behaviour; consumer behaviour in the digital marketplace
  • Data-driven segmentation, targeting, and micro-personalization
  • Consumer motivation and personality in digital environments
  • Consumer perception in digital environments
  • Consumer learning: from traditional theories to AI applications
  • Consumer attitude formation and change through AI-powered persuasion
  • Consumer decision-making processes in digital environments

  • Digital communities, influencer ecosystems, and electronic word-of-mouth

DSMM 330

  • Predictive analytics I
